claim: `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` was raised from 500 to 5000. Nothing in REQ-2283 asks for this. A tenfold higher nesting limit on the untrusted-data preset lets a deeply nested hostile payload recurse much further through formatters. That can cause a StackOverflowException, which cannot be caught and kills the process. This undoes a deliberate secure-by-default limit (ledger L9: depth limit of 500).

claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not in this compilation. That includes MsgPack004 (MemberNeedsKey) raised for a public member inherited from a base class in a referenced assembly by a [MessagePackObject] type declared in source. The type being serialized belongs to this compilation, so ledger L8 (metadata types are not analysed) does not cover it. Before the change this case crashed. Now it produces no diagnostic, even though the member still has no key. The wrapper also drops any diagnostic created with a null location (Location.None) for source types, for example where GetParameterListLocation returns null for an implicitly declared constructor. These could instead be reported at the derived type's identifier.

claim: The wrapper around reportDiagnostic now drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. This includes diagnostics created with a null location (Location.None), for example MemberNeedsKey via FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(). It also includes diagnostics that previously targeted other locations. Users could silently lose diagnostics they get today, such as MsgPack003/004/005 on locations that are not in source. The wrapper applies to all diagnostics, not just the crashing paths.

claim: MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData raises MaximumObjectGraphDepth from 500 to 5000, a tenfold weakening of the recursion depth limit for untrusted data. It is unrelated to the generator/analyzer crash requirement. Deeply nested payloads (arrays or maps nested ~5000 levels) are now accepted, which raises stack-overflow and DoS risk, especially in recursive formatters or on small-stack threads. The ledger's L12 answer is only 'follow the requirement', and the requirement does not mention this setting, so it is out of scope.

claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wraps every reportDiagnostic call and silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the compilation. This includes diagnostics created with a null location from FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), such as MemberNeedsKey (MsgPack004). Diagnostics that warn about insecure or invalid configurations are no longer reported for symbols without source. This is consistent with ledger L8 (referenced-assembly types are deliberately not analysed), so the impact is low. The filter is broad, though: any other diagnostic created with Location.None would also be dropped silently.
